title: Life-expectancy summary (real CC-BY prose from Our World in Data)

source.attribution: Our World in Data (Roser, Ortiz-Ospina, Ritchie), CC-BY-4.0
source.notes: Composed from real Our World in Data life-expectancy figures (CC-BY): newborn 32y (1900) more than doubled to 71y (2021); global ~70y in 2021, less than half two centuries earlier; French 15-year-olds 58 more years (1816) rising to 83 (2021). Clean version verified internally consistent before injecting 3 defects findable from the text's own numbers.

construction.proposer: opus-4.8 (proposed); audited & confirmed 2026-07-05 via oracle audit (validator + anchor-resolution + real/findable/unique pass, docs/oracle-audit-2026-07-05.md) with a targeted human audit of ambiguous/interacting defects and all gray zones (docs/human-audit-checklist)

clean_regions.note: the 1900 newborn figure of 32 years is the real, untouched value
the global 2021 figure of just over 70 years is real and untouched
the 1816 French 15-year-old figure of 58 more years is real and untouched

known_gray_zone.note: '58 more years' is remaining (not total) life expectancy for a 15-year-old; a reviewer may misread it as a total. Phrasing quirk from the source, not a seeded defect.
